graders.name: 03-finding-cites-contradicted-source-point
graders.evidence:
## Verdict
- changes required
- Blocking findings: 3

## Findings
- P1
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md, section 2 (Scope), first bullet ("This batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of the four reviewer roles — code, security, document and coordinator...")
  - Evidence: fixtures/source-notes.md point 4 — the coordinator role's existing case (`coordinator-explore-then-ask`) was left untouched, no new case was added for it, and it does not pair a planted defect with a control section the way the three new cases do
  - Suggestion: "This batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of three reviewer roles — code, security and document — pairing each planted defect with a correct control section in the same fixture. The coordinator role's existing case is unchanged and out of scope for this batch."

- P2
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md, section 3 (Acceptance criteria), AC-01 and AC-02 ("Each of the four cases has a positive grader that detects the planted defect" / "...a negative grader confirming its control section is not wrongly flagged")
  - Evidence: fixtures/source-notes.md point 4 — the coordinator's existing case has no planted defect/control pair, so no grader can verify a planted defect or control section for it; a builder implementing AC-01/AC-02 against "four cases" would attempt to write a grader for a defect that does not exist in the coordinator case
  - Suggestion: change "four cases" to "three cases" in AC-01 and AC-02, or add a distinct, separately-stated criterion for the coordinator case if one is intended.

- P3
  - Category: gap
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md, section 2 (Scope), second bullet ("Each case's fixtures are copied into the run workspace before the run by the case's own scaffold script, so no case depends on a shared fixture directory.")
  - Evidence: fixtures/source-notes.md point 6 — the scaffold.sh is "invoked only when the runner is passed `--scaffold`"; the document drops this condition and implies scaffolding happens automatically before every run
  - Suggestion: "Each new case's fixtures are copied into the run workspace by the case's own scaffold.sh, invoked only when the runner is passed --scaffold, so no case depends on a shared fixture directory."

## Not raised
- Source points 1–3 (code, security, document seeded-defect cases) map correctly to the scope bullet naming those three roles.
- Source point 5 (planted defect paired with a correct control section in the same fixture) is accurately carried for the three genuinely new cases.
- AC-01 and AC-02 wording is itself observable (grader detects/confirms a concrete outcome), not subjective — checked as a weak-criterion candidate and found sound in wording, independent of the scope conflict in P2.
- References section correctly cites source-notes.md; no unsourced (excess) requirement found in scope or acceptance criteria beyond the four-role overclaim already flagged.
- Identifiers AC-01/AC-02 are unique and sequential; no duplicate or misfiled section found — organization category checked, no finding.
- No ambiguous sentence found that two builders would implement differently in a way that changes behavior, beyond the gap/conflict items already raised.

## Evidence
- Files read: fixtures/source-notes.md, fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md.
- No previous review report exists at fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md.review.md — treated as round 1.
- All six mandatory categories (gaps, ambiguities, conflicts, excesses, weak criteria, organization) were checked against the source-to-document map built from source-notes.md points 1–6 against PRD-scope-claim.md sections 2–4.

graders.name: 03-finding-cites-contradicted-source-point
graders.evidence:
## Verdict
- changes required
- Blocking findings: 3
- Report: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md.review.md

## Findings
- P1
  - Category: conflict
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md section 2 (Scope), bullet 1
  - Evidence: The document states "this batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of the four reviewer roles — code, security, document and coordinator — pairing each planted defect with a correct control section in the same fixture." source-notes.md point 4 states the coordinator role's existing case "was left untouched — no new case was added for it in this batch, and it does not pair a planted defect with a control section the way the three new cases do." Only three new cases were added (points 1–3); the coordinator case is pre-existing and lacks the defect/control pairing.
  - Suggestion: Correct the scope to state that this batch adds one seeded-defect eval case for each of three reviewer roles — code, security and document — each pairing a planted defect with a control section, and that the coordinator role's existing case is unchanged and out of scope for this batch.
  - Reported by: claude
- P2
  - Category: weak criterion
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md section 3 (Acceptance criteria), AC-01 and AC-02
  - Evidence: AC-01 and AC-02 require a positive grader (detecting the planted defect) and a negative grader (confirming the control section is not wrongly flagged) for "each of the four cases." Per source-notes.md point 4, the coordinator's existing case has neither a planted defect nor a control section, so no such grader can be built or observed as passing/failing for that case.
  - Suggestion: Scope AC-01 and AC-02 to the three new cases (code-reviewer-form-check, security-reviewer-authz-check, document-validator-overclaim-check) only, and drop or separately state that the coordinator case requires no new grader.
  - Reported by: claude
- P3
  - Category: gap
  - Severity: blocking
  - Location: fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md section 2 (Scope), bullet 2
  - Evidence: The document states fixtures "are copied into the run workspace before the run by the case's own scaffold script," with no gating condition. source-notes.md point 6 states this copy step is "invoked only when the runner is passed `--scaffold`." The opt-in condition is dropped.
  - Suggestion: State explicitly that each case's scaffold.sh copies its fixtures into the run workspace only when the runner is invoked with `--scaffold`.
  - Reported by: claude

## Not raised
- source-notes.md points 1–3 (new code/security/document cases): correctly represented within scope bullet 1, apart from the "four roles" miscount flagged in P1.
- source-notes.md point 5 (defect/control pairing per new case, resisting keyword-only detection): correctly reflected in scope bullet 1 for the three real new cases.
- Organization: AC-01 and AC-02 identifiers are unique, sequential, and filed under the correct section; no duplication found.
- Excess: no requirement in the document lacks a corresponding source point beyond the miscounts already flagged as conflicts/gap; References section cites only source-notes.md, matching the actual source provided.
- Ambiguity: language for the three genuinely-new cases is specific enough that two builders would implement the same scope, aside from the issues already raised in P1–P3.

## Evidence
- Files read: fixtures/source-notes.md (source, 11 lines), fixtures/PRD-scope-claim.md (document, 31 lines).
- No previous review report exists next to the document; this is round 1.
